verdict: THE JUDGE READS OVERLAP, CAUSALLY. Appending six distinctive tokens from response A rather than from B moves the judge's A-vs-B satisfaction gap by +0.2507 [+0.2300,+0.2714] for the SAME criterion. The appendage is the same kind of object in both arms, so its semantic effect cancels; what differs is only which response donated the words. The unrelated-token null is -0.0045 [-0.01814146985685131, 0.009380959221030993], spanning zero, so this is the SOURCE of the tokens and not the act of appending. r51's +0.2068 correlation now has a demonstrated mechanism, and r50's anchoring effect has a concrete instrument explanation. BOUND, NOT EQUALITY: this shows overlap-sensitivity on PERTURBED text; natural high-overlap criteria are not perturbed and this does not measure the judge's behaviour on them
outcome_variable_scope: Descriptive on the judge's own outputs under intervention. No human rankings and no preference proxy enter this round.
scope: Interventional on the judge. Shows overlap-sensitivity on PERTURBED criterion text -- a criterion with a token list glued to it is not a natural criterion, so this BOUNDS the judge's overlap sensitivity rather than measuring its behaviour on naturally high-overlap criteria. Token rarity is a live alternative to token matching, addressed only partly by the unrelated-donor arm whose tokens are equally rare.
